questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Recommendations from friends, the nature, the ability to speak with inhabitants and i just find Norway fascinating.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Hmm not that difficult if you make an effort. But it can be a little anxiety-provoking when you dont know if you done everything you should.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from other students. Other than that, the social science exchange students (geography is social science in Norway) were included in the introduction week for new students, called fadderuken. It was really confusing because nobody knew anything about it and i (as a third year student) was included in fadderuken for new students hahah. But it was a lot of fun, like rusuge in Denmark and a nice way to get to know Norwegians and exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The information from the study was ok but the whole thing about fadderuken was confusing. And also the fact that social science had the fadderuke but humanistics and natural science didn't. They didn't give any reason for this.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. Everyone who wants student housing get housing at Fantoft.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is like an exchange student city which is nice! but it is also placed outside the city centre

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice and easy to be social. You most likely share a room with one other person which Sammen could specify more. But it is nice and social.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can apply for as many courses you want and just decline them later after the first study week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Hmm pretty normal, cant really remember

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I called UIB who were really helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was a little late registrering but i got 2 really nice courses and one which i just had to take to get ects.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time and sign up for more courses than what you need

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was high. Pretty much the samme as copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: GEO217 and KOGVIT101 was pretty much the same as copenhagen with lectures and seminars. But GEO313 was really nice with a 4 day field trip and 4 days laboratory work which was really nice and insightful in real scientific work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEO217 - Hydrology, Ground Water and Geohazards
GEO313 - Field and Laboratory Methods in Physical Geography
KOGVIT101 - Introduction to the Cognitive Sciences

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: GEO313 - Field and Laboratory Methods in Physical Geography. A lot of practical teaching and down to earth teachers who are really skilled.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: BSI host a lot of nice things.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Found a local football club called SK trane were i played. I took part in BSI monday running which i really enjoyed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Monday running

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for a hike

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Norwegians and Danes are alike.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm take part in voluntary work (maybe some festivals) or study related things.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The prizing hahah. And then i found it difficult that Norwegians dont have the same bar/pub culture as in Denmark. You drink at home and then you go out dancing mostly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The use of the nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to nice places

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go. Bergen is a nice city with a lot of cultural events and the most beautiful nature. The university is also good.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying new things and meeting people from allover the world. It gives a new perspective to your life in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it hard to be a part of the Norwegian life in Bergen. Maybe it would be easier if i lived in the city centre with some norwegians

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
